tools.name: Remove Contact from Automation
tools.description: Removes a contact from a specified automation in ActiveCampaign. This action looks up the contact by their email address to get their ID, then removes them from the specified automation. A contact can be enrolled in the same automation multiple times (different runs), and you can choose to remove them from all runs or just the most recent run using the run_remove_option parameter. Use this when you need to unenroll a contact from an automation workflow they're currently enrolled in. This is a destructive operation that cannot be undone. Technical details: Uses /api/3/contacts to find the contact, /api/3/contactAutomations to list their enrollments, and DELETE /api/3/contactAutomations/{id} to remove each enrollment.

parameters.description: Specifies which automation runs to remove. Use 'all' to remove the contact from all instances of this automation (if they were enrolled multiple times), or 'latest' to remove only from the most recent enrollment. Default is 'all'.

tools.name: Track Event in ActiveCampaign
tools.description: Track custom events for contacts in ActiveCampaign to trigger automations and monitor user engagement. This action records specific user actions (e.g., file downloads, button clicks, logins) for existing contacts. Events can be used to trigger automation workflows in ActiveCampaign. Prerequisites: - Event Tracking must be enabled in ActiveCampaign (Settings > Tracking > Site Tracking) - The contact must already exist in ActiveCampaign - Event names should be whitelisted in ActiveCampaign for automation usage Use cases: - Track user behavior on your website or application - Trigger targeted email campaigns based on user actions - Monitor engagement and build user profiles - Create conditional automation workflows

parameters.name: event_key
parameters.description: Your Event Key from ActiveCampaign. Find this in Settings > Tracking > Event Tracking in your ActiveCampaign account. It's a long alphanumeric string (e.g., 'c12973b078007927842301eff932e7d78b74b3e').

parameters.name: event_name
parameters.description: Name of the event to track (max 32 characters). This identifies the type of action being recorded. For automation triggers, ensure the event name is whitelisted in your ActiveCampaign automations. Use descriptive, consistent naming (e.g., 'file_download', 'purchase_complete', 'trial_started').

parameters.name: event_actid
parameters.description: Your ActiveCampaign Account ID (actid). Find this in Settings > Tracking > Event Tracking API (click the button to see the modal with your actid). It's typically a 9-10 digit number.

parameters.name: event_value
parameters.description: Optional additional data to store with the event. Can be used to pass context like URLs, product names, transaction IDs, or any relevant string value. This data can be referenced later in automations.

parameters.name: event_contact_email
parameters.description: Email address of the contact for whom the event is being tracked. Must be an existing contact in ActiveCampaign.

Important notes: - Only the 'name' field is reliably updateable via this endpoint - The API typically returns HTTP 204 (No Content) on success - Group must exist or will return 404 error Use 'Get All Groups' or 'Get Group by ID' actions to find the group ID first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the group to update. Can be found using the 'Get All Groups' or 'Get Group by ID' actions.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: New name for the group. This is the primary field you should update. Must be a non-empty string if provided.

tools.name: Update Order
tools.description: Updates an existing order in the ActiveTrail commerce system. Use this action to modify order details including customer information (name, email, phone), shipping address, order status, pricing (amounts, tax, currency), or product items. You must provide the existing order_id - this action cannot create new orders. Common use cases: - Update order status (e.g., from "pending" to "shipped") - Modify customer contact information - Adjust pricing or add/remove items - Update shipping addresses - Change order metadata (dates, custom fields)

parameters.name: tax
parameters.description: Total tax amount applied to this order (VAT, sales tax, etc.)

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: Shipping address city name

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Customer's email address for order communications and receipts

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: List of products/items included in this order. Each item can have quantity, price, and product details

parameters.name: mobile
parameters.description: Customer's mobile phone number (include country code for international numbers)

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Current order fulfillment status. Common values: pending, processing, completed, shipped, cancelled, refunded

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Customer's shipping street address (number and street name)

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: Optional: Order identifier to include in the request body. Usually the same as order_id. Only include if you want to change the order ID itself

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this order

parameters.name: lastName
parameters.description: Customer's last (family) name

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the order to update. This value is used in the API URL path (e.g., /commerce/Order/{order_id})

parameters.name: firstName
parameters.description: Customer's first (given) name

parameters.name: netAmount
parameters.description: Subtotal amount before tax is applied (sum of item prices minus discounts)

parameters.name: orderName
parameters.description: Custom display name or reference label for this order (for internal tracking)

parameters.name: totalPrice
parameters.description: Total order price before tax (deprecated: use totalAmount instead)

parameters.name: totalAmount
parameters.description: Final grand total amount (netAmount + tax + any additional fees)

parameters.name: purchaseDate
parameters.description: Date and time when the order was placed. Format: ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with optional timezone)

tools.name: Update Template
tools.description: Tool to update an existing email template in ActiveTrail account. Use this action to modify template properties including: - Template name and subject line - HTML content/body - Editor type and display settings - Template categorization - Character encoding settings All fields except 'id' are optional - only provide the fields you want to update. The template will be updated with the new values while preserving any fields not specified. Note: To update only the HTML content of a template, consider using the 'Update Template Content' action instead.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the template to update

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Template name. Update this to change the template's display name.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: HTML or text content of the template. Update this to change the template's body content.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Email subject line. Update this to change the default subject for emails using this template.

parameters.name: editor_type
parameters.description: Template editor type. Specifies which editor was used to create the template. Common values: 'HTML' for HTML editor, 'WYSIWYG' for visual editor, 'DragAndDrop' for drag-and-drop builder.

parameters.name: AddPrintButton
parameters.description: Whether to add a print button to the email template. When true, recipients can print the email directly from their email client.

parameters.name: campaign_encoding
parameters.description: Character encoding for the email campaign. Determines how text is encoded in the email. Common values: 0 for UTF-8 (recommended for international characters), 1 for ISO-8859-1 (Western European), 2 for Windows-1255 (Hebrew).

parameters.name: template_category_id
parameters.description: Category identifier for organizing templates. Use this to categorize templates (e.g., newsletters, promotions, transactional). You can get valid category IDs from the 'Get Content Categories' action.

parameters.name: event_value_type
parameters.description: How the parameter value is determined. Valid values: 'custom_text' (use static value from 'value' field), 'user_field' (dynamically use contact field specified in 'user_field').

parameters.name: event_parameter_type
parameters.description: Where the parameter will be sent. Valid values: 'header' (HTTP header), 'query' (URL query parameter), 'body' (request body field).

tools.name: Delete Data Points
tools.description: Permanently delete 1-30 feed data points sequentially through Adafruit IO's single-data-point DELETE endpoint, bounded by the Free-plan limit of 30 data mutations per minute. This operation is not atomic: each ID has an independent outcome, and successful earlier deletions are not rolled back. Processing may continue after an independent malformed-ID or not-found response, but stops after authentication, permission, rate-limit, server, unexpected, or ambiguous transport failures; remaining IDs are marked not_attempted.

tools.name: Core-plan completion decision

Use this tool when the system has proposed a plan step that requires user confirmation before it can be executed — such as creating an audience, a journey, a campaign, or any other entity. This is the final step that completes the plan.

- The system is waiting for the user's decision to proceed with a plan
- The user provides an explicit approve or reject response to a pending proposal

- User says "reject", "cancel", "don't create it", "decline", "stop"

Parameters:
- decision (required): "approve" to confirm and execute the plan, "reject" to cancel it

Returns the final orchestrator response confirming the plan was completed or cancelled.

tools.name: Create Document
tools.description: Upload a document to Affinda for parsing and data extraction. Use this action when you need to: - Parse resumes/CVs to extract candidate information - Process invoices to extract line items, amounts, and vendor details - Extract data from any supported document type (PDF, DOCX, images) You can upload either a file directly or provide a publicly accessible URL. The document will be processed by Affinda's AI extraction engine. Prerequisites: - For collection-based uploads: Get collection ID from get_collections action - For workspace-specific uploads: Get workspace ID from get_workspaces action

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Publicly accessible URL of the document to parse. Alternative to uploading a `file`. The URL must be directly accessible without authentication.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Document file to upload for parsing. Supports PDF, DOCX, DOC, PNG, JPG, TIFF formats.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: If true, the API will wait for parsing to complete before returning. If false or omitted, returns immediately with status 'pending'.

parameters.name: compact
parameters.description: If true, return a compact response with fewer fields for faster transmission.

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: Override filename when uploading via URL. This sets the document's display name in Affinda. Ignored when uploading via `file` parameter.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: ISO 639-1 language code for the document content. Helps improve OCR and extraction accuracy for non-English documents.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Workspace identifier where the document will be created. Obtain this from the get_workspaces action. If omitted, defaults to the user's primary workspace.

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: Collection identifier to add the document to. Obtain this from the get_collections action. If not specified, document will be in the workspace without a collection.

parameters.name: expiryTime
parameters.description: ISO 8601 datetime when the document should be automatically deleted. Use for temporary documents or compliance requirements.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: Custom identifier for your own reference to track this document. Must be unique within your workspace.

parameters.name: rejectDuplicates
parameters.description: If true, reject the document if it appears to be a duplicate of an existing document in the collection.

tools.name: Create Validation Result
tools.description: Create a validation result for document annotations in Affinda. Use this tool to record validation outcomes after parsing a document. Validation results track whether specific annotations (extracted data fields) pass or fail business rules. Prerequisites: 1. Get a document identifier from Get Documents or Create Document 2. Get annotation IDs from Get Annotations for that document 3. Define a kebab-case rule slug that identifies your validation rule Example use cases: - Recording that an invoice total matches the sum of line items - Marking that a required field is present and valid - Logging validation failures for review workflows

parameters.name: passed
parameters.description: Whether the validation passed (true), failed (false), or is not applicable (null/omitted).

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Human-readable message explaining why the validation passed or failed.

parameters.name: document
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the document being validated. Obtain from Get Documents or Create Document actions.

parameters.name: ruleSlug
parameters.description: The kebab-case slug identifier of the validation rule being applied. Must match pattern: lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only (e.g., 'field-is-required', 'amount-is-positive').

parameters.name: annotations
parameters.description: List of annotation IDs that this validation result applies to. Obtain annotation IDs from the Get Annotations action for a specific document.

tools.name: Batch Create Validation Results
tools.description: Batch create multiple validation results for document annotations in a single API call. Use this action to efficiently record validation outcomes for multiple documents or rules at once, rather than making individual create requests for each validation result. This is particularly useful for bulk validation workflows or when validating multiple rules across many documents. Prerequisites: - Obtain document identifiers from Get Documents or Create Document actions - Get annotation IDs from Get Annotations for those documents - Define kebab-case rule slugs that identify your validation rules Common use cases: - Bulk recording of validation results across multiple documents - Validating multiple business rules on the same document - Automated validation workflows for large document batches

tools.name: Update Annotation
tools.description: Tool to update data of a single annotation in Affinda. Use when you need to correct extracted values, verify annotations, or modify annotation metadata after document processing. Prerequisites: - Obtain the annotation ID using the 'Get Annotations' action with a document filter - Annotations must exist in documents that have been processed by Affinda Common use cases: - Correcting OCR or extraction errors in individual fields - Marking annotations as verified after manual review (set isClientVerified=true) - Updating parsed values to fix incorrect data extraction - Modifying annotation coordinates or page references Note: For bulk updates across multiple annotations, use the 'Batch Update Annotations' action instead for better efficiency.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the annotation to update. Obtain annotation IDs from the 'Get Annotations' action by filtering on a specific document.

parameters.name: raw
parameters.description: Raw text extracted from the document before any post-processing. This is the original OCR or text extraction result.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: Field identifier to categorize this annotation. Can be null if not associated with a specific field.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: The parent annotation's ID if this annotation is nested or hierarchical. Set to null if this is a top-level annotation.

parameters.name: parsed
parameters.description: The parsed/processed value for the annotation. This is the extracted or corrected data value after processing. Type varies based on the annotation's content type (string, integer, number, boolean, object, or array).

parameters.name: document
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for the document this annotation belongs to.

parameters.name: dataPoint
parameters.description: Data point identifier to update. This links the annotation to a specific field in the document schema.

parameters.name: pageIndex
parameters.description: The page number within the document where this annotation appears, starting from 0.

parameters.name: rectangles
parameters.description: Array of x/y coordinate rectangles containing the annotation data on the document. An annotation can span multiple rectangles (e.g., text wrapping across lines).

parameters.name: isClientVerified
parameters.description: Set to true to mark the annotation as verified by a human. Use this after manual review to confirm the extracted data is correct.

parameters.name: validationResults
parameters.description: The validation results created, changed or deleted as a result of updating the annotation. Typically managed by the system automatically.

tools.name: Authenticate for JWT via V4 SSO
tools.description: Completes AgencyZoom V4 Single Sign-On (SSO) authentication by exchanging an OAuth2 authorization code for a JWT token. Prerequisites: First call get_auth_url_for_v4sso to obtain the authentication URL, then redirect the user to that URL for login. After successful authentication through Vertafore's OAuth provider, the callback will include a 'code' parameter. Use that code with this action to obtain the JWT token for API access. Note: This is typically used during initial authentication setup. The code is single-use, time-limited, and must match the PKCE challenge from the original auth request.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: OAuth2 authorization code received from the V4SSO callback after user authentication through Vertafore login. This code is obtained by redirecting the user to the auth URL from GET /v1/api/v4sso/get-auth-params, where they authenticate, and the OAuth provider redirects back with this code parameter. The code is single-use and time-limited.

tools.name: Update policy by id
tools.description: Updates an existing insurance policy for the given `policyId`; monetary values must be in cents and dates in YYYY-MM-DD format.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: Number of items covered (e.g., vehicles for auto policy, properties for property policy).

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the agent or producer who sold the policy.

parameters.name: premium
parameters.description: Total premium amount for the policy term, in cents (e.g., $123.45 is 12345).

parameters.name: policyId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the policy to be updated (specified in the request path).

parameters.name: soldDate
parameters.description: Date policy was sold or bound (Format: YYYY-MM-DD).

parameters.name: brokerFee
parameters.description: Broker fee for the policy, in cents (e.g., $50.00 is 5000).

parameters.name: carrierId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the insurance carrier.

parameters.name: groupCode
parameters.description: Code to associate the policy with a specific group for internal tracking or reporting.

parameters.name: expiryDate
parameters.description: Date policy coverage ends (Format: YYYY-MM-DD).

parameters.name: policyType
parameters.description: Identifier for the type of policy transaction (e.g., New Business, Renewal).

parameters.name: insuredName
parameters.description: Name(s) of the insured party or parties (individual or company).

parameters.name: agencyNumber
parameters.description: Identifier for the agency branch or location associated with this policy.

parameters.name: leadSourceId
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the lead source (e.g., referral, website).

parameters.name: policyNumber
parameters.description: Unique alphanumeric string assigned to the policy by the insurance carrier.

parameters.name: effectiveDate
parameters.description: Date policy coverage begins (Format: YYYY-MM-DD).

parameters.name: departmentCode
parameters.description: Code to assign the policy to a specific department (e.g., Personal Lines, Commercial Lines).

parameters.name: priorExpiryDate
parameters.description: Expiry date of the previous policy (Format: YYYY-MM-DD), if applicable.

parameters.name: priorCarrierName
parameters.description: Name of the previous insurance company, if applicable.

parameters.name: priorPolicyNumber
parameters.description: Policy number of the previous insurance policy, if applicable.

parameters.name: productCategoryId
parameters.description: Identifier for the policy's product category (e.g., Auto, Home, Commercial).
